title: Orchestrated model trial supervisor and auto-revert policy for safe rollouts
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Build an orchestration layer and control-plane primitives to run A/B/canary/shadow experiments for model versions with automated exposure control and statistically-sound early rollback. The feature ("OrchestratedModelTrial") should let PM/Eng define an experiment manifest (variants, cohorts, metrics, success criteria, exposure budget, duration) and take control actions automatically (increase/decrease exposure, stop, revert to previous variant) when pre-specified signals are triggered. This ticket covers the product spec, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and coordination with eng/design for Phase 1 MVP.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Experiment manifest schema defined and stored: variants, cohort selectors, primary/secondary metrics, minimum sample sizes, schedule windows, exposure budget (percentage/time), and abort thresholds.
2) Backend scheduler that can enact staged exposure (e.g., 0.1% -> 1% -> 10%) and holdpoints for statistical checks between steps.
3) Automatic early-stop and auto-revert implemented that triggers on preconfigured statistical checks (see statistical_checks) and can flip traffic back to a safe variant within SLA latency targets.
4) Console UI to create/inspect experiments, visualize metric trajectories (latency, cost, quality), and a manual override/kickstart control for operators.
5) End-to-end tests and canary simulation harness validate behavior across flakey latency and synthetic drift scenarios.
6) Playbook and runbook documentation in Confluence and a safe default policy for new tenants.
7) Instrumentation emits rollout events, decision reasons, and raw aggregated metrics to existing dashboards for auditing and postmortems.
tasks: PM: finalize manifest field list and default safety budgets
Eng: design and implement staged exposure scheduler and execution API
Eng: implement sequential statistical monitor (Bayesian posterior & frequentist SPRT prototype) as pluggable module
Design: wireframe experiment creation and a compact experiment inspector UI
Eng: add audit logging and decision rationale to event stream
Eng: integrate with routing layer (smart routing) to apply traffic splits and shadow traffic forwarding
QA: build simulated-traffic harness and write e2e tests for early-stop behaviors
Docs: publish playbook and operator runbook in Confluence
SRE: define SLOs for rollback time and failure modes
engineering_notes: Prefer pluggable statistical engines: implement a light Bayesian posterior check first for smoother early-stop handling; prototype SPRT for very low-latency binary metrics.
KV-cache and batching interactions: when traffic is reduced or shifted, preserve session affinities to avoid user-visible regressions.
Rollout commands are idempotent and must be replayable from audit stream for disaster recovery.
Edge case: model variant that uses a different tokenizer or output schema must be quarantined to shadow traffic only until compatibility is verified.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (MVP): server-side manifest + basic staged exposure + Bayesian early-stop on primary metric; console read-only view
Phase 1.5: console creation UI, manual override, and shadow traffic routing
Phase 2: cohort-aware phased exposure, multi-metric composite checks, and A/B dashboard with cohort breakdowns
Safety hold: default policy limits peak exposure to 10% during first 48h for new models unless explicitly waived
Release gating: experimental feature behind tenant flag for initial customers
statistical_checks: Primary approach: Bayesian sequential monitor comparing posterior probability that variant > control exceeds threshold (e.g., P(delta < 0) > 0.995 triggers rollback).
Fallback approach: Sequential Probability Ratio Test (SPRT) available for binary metrics with tight latency requirements.
Minimum sample requirement enforced per cohort before any decision (configurable per experiment).
Delay windows for metrics with delayed signal (e.g., downstream conversion) — experiment manifest supports delayed-primary-metric windows.
Graceful degradation: consider latency and error budget signals alongside quality — do not auto-promote if 95th percentile latency increases beyond threshold.
